question: When you look at the front side of a table spoon, an inverted image of yours is formed. The front side of table spoon works as a:
solution:
The Correct answer is __**concave mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The front side of a **table spoon** has a **concave surface**, which means it curves inward.
 
• When you look at the front side of a table spoon, it acts like a **concave mirror**.
 
• **Concave mirrors** reflect light from their inwardly curved surface, focusing light to a point.
 
• These mirrors form an **inverted image** when the object is placed beyond the focal point.
 
• **Concave mirrors** are commonly used in applications where focused light is required, such as in **telescopes**, **headlights**, and **shaving mirrors**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave lens**__

 __
 
• A **concave lens** diverges light rays that pass through it, spreading them apart.
 
• It is used in **corrective glasses** for people with myopia (nearsightedness).
 
 
 
• **Convex mirror**__
 __
 
• A **convex mirror** has an outwardly curved surface and diverges light rays, spreading them out.
 
• It forms a **virtual, upright**, and **diminished image** of objects.
 
• **Convex mirrors** are often used in **vehicle side mirrors** and **security mirrors**.
 
 
 
• **Plane mirror**__
 
 
• A **plane mirror** has a flat reflective surface that forms a **virtual, upright**, and **same-size image** of the object.
 
• Plane mirrors are commonly used in **household mirrors** and **periscopes**.
